To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the technique presented here can be used to generate internal sequence data from less than 10 mg of protein bound to PVDF or nitrocelluose membranes after electophoretic transfer from SDS-PAGE.

the use of hydrogenated Triton as the detergent in the digestion buffer allows the direct recovery of peptides from the digestion of proteins bound to membranes for microsequencing, with high yields and good reproducibility.

we have developed an internal protein sequence analysis technique that is applicable to less than 10-micrograms of protein bound either to PVDF or nitrocelluose after electrophoretical transfer from SDS-PAGE.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of proteins that are difficult or impossible to purify to homogeneity by other methods.
the development and optimization of a method for the enzymatic generation and isolation of peptide fragments from less than 10-micrograms amounts of protein bound to PVDF or nitrocelluose membranes.
the development and application of a new procedure for the generation of internal peptide fragments of membrane-bound proteins for sequence analysis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the method described here has produced internal sequence information for 120 proteins, with a 90% success rate, and that it has been successfully used to sequence proteins with molecular weights from 12,000 to 100,000.
this method is a very powerful and useful technique for internal sequence analysis of proteins.
this technique has been successfully applied to 120 peptides, 90% of which have produced results.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
this technique is a viable method for the generation and purification of internal peptides for proteins less than 10-15 micrograms.

this technique can be used for internal protein sequence analysis of 3.5-10 micrograms of proteins with a minimum of 50% recovery of the internal peptide fragments, with a 20 pmol average initial yield.
the technique is simple, rapid, sensitive, and reproducible, and it is applicable to a wide range of protein samples.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to obtain internal protein sequence data from as little as 3 micrograms of a protein bound to either a PVDF or nitrocelluose membrane.

it is possible to obtain internal sequence data from less than 10 ug of protein, provided that the proteins are transferred to membranes and that they are digested in the presence of a nonionic surfactant, such as 1% Triton X- 100.

PVDF and nitrocellulore membranes are both useful for internal sequence analysis of proteins, and that the use of Triton X-10 in the enzymatic digestion step is a critical step for the successful recovery of internal peptides.
